vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: fund-keeper
Version: 2.7.0

The fund-keeper skill bundle is a functional financial tool designed to track Chinese mutual funds and stocks. It fetches real-time data from legitimate financial providers such as Eastmoney (天天基金), Sina Finance, and AKShare. The code logic, including portfolio management in fund_keeper.py and statistics in fund_stats.py, is consistent with its stated purpose. While it includes dependencies like easyocr for image recognition and mentions pyautogui in metadata, there is no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches a fund/stock/OCR tool but contains incoherent requirements and cross-skill/file assumptions (pyautogui listed but not used, references to other skills and absolute user paths), so review before installing or running with real data.

dimensions.detail: The name/description and code implement finance, stock, and OCR features and request network access — that is coherent. However SKILL.md/metadata lists pyautogui as a required binary while none of the provided Python files reference pyautogui; this is a mismatch. The skill also documents explicit calls to scripts in another skill (stock-analysis) which creates an implicit dependency on another skill's files.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are consistent with a CLI tool: install Python deps, place files under the skills dir, and run commands. The code reads/writes files under a funds/ directory (within the skill or a workspace fallback) and uses network APIs to fetch market data — expected for this purpose. Notes of concern: several scripts use absolute default paths (e.g., C:\Users\Administrator\.openclaw\media\inbound\...) and SKILL.md suggests invoking scripts in ~/.openclaw/skills/stock-analysis, which means the skill assumes and may access other skill directories or user paths.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automated install spec (instruction-only in registry), and dependencies are standard Python packages (akshare, pandas, requests, easyocr). This is lower risk than arbitrary binary downloads. INSTALL.md warns EasyOCR models will be downloaded (~100MB), which is expected for OCR but should be noted.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables or credentials (good). It does require network permission (package.json) which is appropriate for fetching market data. The declared required binary pyautogui is unexplained (not used in included files) — request for a GUI automation binary without justification is disproportionate. The skill also references external skill scripts (stock-analysis) and will operate on files under parent directories, which broadens its filesystem reach.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request elevated privileges. It creates and updates files under a funds/ folder (config, cache, history) which is normal for a local CLI skill. The SKILL.md suggests adding cron tasks via openclaw CLI; scheduling itself is optional and user-driven.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to implement the advertised fund/stock/OCR functionality, but a few things don't add up: 1) the metadata lists pyautogui though none of the scripts use it — ask the author why or remove that requirement; 2) the skill assumes other skill files (stock-analysis) and uses absolute user paths, so it may read files outside its own folder — run it in a sandbox first; 3) OCR (easyocr) will download large model files and the skill requires network access to fetch market data. Before installing on a machine with sensitive data: inspect/grep the full code for any unexpected network endpoints or credential usage, run it in an isolated environment, and avoid granting it access to credentials or production workspaces until you confirm behavior. If you want, I can point to the specific lines/places that reference other-skill paths and absolute paths or search the code for pyautogui references.
